column2: How do I note the illnesses and known causes of death in the family (🩺 Family health)?
column3: It is hidden at first, because it is private: Settings → Data → “🩺 Family health” → “Show”. On the record, the “🩺 Health” block (arranged like the other blocks): “＋ Add” an illness, a disability, a cause of death or an epidemic lived through, with its date (as in a record), its source, a note and “To check”. The cause written on the death record appears there by itself, and the epidemics during the person’s lifetime (“🌍 The world around”) are noted in one click. The whole family: Lists → “🩺 Family health”. This is family memory: the app gives no advice and calculates no risk.

column2: How do I see an illness across the branches of the family?
column3: Lists → “🩺 Family health” → “🌳 By branches” tab (or the “🌳 By branches” button of the 🩺 block on the record): choose the person at the centre and the illness with the picker. The fan of ancestors colours those in whom it is noted; “The four sides” sorts these people by grandparent. Only numbers of people, never a percentage.

column2: Does family health go into my exports?
column3: No. It is never in the website, family sharing, packages, books, simple mode, games, or when printing the record; when hidden, it does not appear in search either, and nothing shows in view-only mode 🔒. Only GEDCOM can carry it, if you tick “🩺 Include family health” when exporting. The causes written on death records remain events, exported as before.

column2: How do I see the guided tour (first steps) again?
column3: Settings → “FAQ / guide” → “▶ Restart the guided tour” (or type “tour” in the quick search). In 6 steps, the app circles the real buttons: create a record, add a parent, add a photo, add an event and its place, make a backup, find Settings and the FAQ. Click the circled button to do it for real (the tour waits until you have finished), or “Next” to just look; “Previous”, “Skip the tour”, and on the keyboard → ← Esc. A step whose button is hidden (locked record, hidden block) is skipped. The tour is offered once at first launch; it never opens in simple mode or view-only mode.

column2: What is the first-launch screen for (“I want to do something else”, sample database)?
column3: The very first time an empty database is opened, under “Create and open the database”, the link “I want to do something else ▾” offers 9 uses (🌳 genealogy, 🐾 animal lineage, 🔭 counting animals, 🏠 house or village, 🎨 artist, 📚 archives, 🔤 surname, 🏭 company, ✨ memories): the app then only shows the useful tabs, without deleting anything. You can also import (Hérédis, MacFamilyTree, GEDCOM), “Start with an empty database” or “🧪 Try with a sample database”: an imaginary family (5 generations, nobody born after 1950, nobody living) kept separately in “My genealogies”, with a “🧪 Sample database” banner to go back to your genealogy. To change later: Settings → Appearance → Menus → “🧭 How you use the app” (several uses at once, “First screen on opening”, “🧭 See the first launch again”).

column2: What was the weather on the day of a birth, a marriage or a death (weather of the past)?
column3: On the record, under the place of each event, a small “🌦” badge gives the icon and the temperature (at the hour of the record if known, otherwise in the afternoon). On hover: a sentence (“It was very cold: −6 °C in the morning…”) and the reliability; on click: the day in 4 moments (since 1940), the comparison with the 30-year normal, the station, the days around, the source. The date must be known to the day and the place must be placed on the map. Everything works without the Internet: the data is in the app (the base set) or in a pack imported once. Old weather remains an estimate: it helps you imagine the day, it does not replace the record.

column2: What do “Measured”, “Station 31 km away”, “Estimated” and “Rough reconstruction” mean?
column3: “Measured”: a station less than 15 km away (and less than 150 m difference in altitude) took readings that day. “Station … km away”: the nearest is between 15 and 40 km away, so it is indicative; rain becomes “it rained in the area”, because it changes quickly from one village to the next. “Estimated (grid cell ≈ 30 km)”: no station close enough, the value comes from the ERA5 reanalysis (1940 → today). “Rough reconstruction”: from 1836 to 1939, the 20CR reanalysis (≈ 100 km), hidden until you ask for it in the settings. Before that, or with nothing: “No known reading near here before 1863 (first station: Toulouse)”.

column2: How do I compare two old maps of the same area (two periods)?
column3: Map → “⇆ Compare” button (top bar): on the left the background you usually choose, on the right a second background (“Right”: Cassini, État-Major, IGN 1950…). “▏ Line”: drag the white line (or the ← → arrows on the keyboard); “◫ Side by side”: the two backgrounds next to each other, centred on the same spot (the points are hidden); “◐ Transparency”: the second background on top, with adjustable transparency. × closes the comparison; the choice is remembered.

column2: How do I see the provinces before 1789, the departments of 1790 or vanished communes on the map?
column3: Map → “🏛 Borders ▾”: tick “Provinces of the Ancien Régime”, “Departments of 1790”, “Vanished or merged communes” (and, if you like, renamed communes). A click on an area or a circle gives its name, its date and, for a vanished commune, its present-day commune. The provinces and departments of 1790 are APPROXIMATE outlines drawn from today’s departments (there is no free official source of their real outlines). Vanished communes come from the official INSEE history (since 1943), to download once.

column2: Where are the old borders (vanished communes)?
column3: They come with the app: two official INSEE files (Code officiel géographique 2026, Licence Ouverte 2.0, 5.5 MB), installed by themselves and checked by their fingerprint, without the Internet, for all your genealogies. Settings → “🏛 Old borders” shows their size, their fingerprint and their licence; “⤓ Install the old borders” puts them back if you removed them. The old names of communes also help the place picker (“formerly “…””). “🗑 Remove” takes them away, with “↶ Undo”.

column2: How do I see where a surname is concentrated, century by century?
column3: Charts → New → Maps → “🔤 Surname map” → “From the app” tab: choose the name in the list (the most frequent first) or a person (their name is used), then “Use this data”. Coloured departments or circles per place; the ▶ slider under the drawing goes through the centuries one by one. Never a living person or a confidential record.

column2: How do I see on a map the places of the ancestors I share with my DNA cousins?
column3: Charts → New → Maps → “🧬 DNA cousins map” → “From the app”: choose the DNA test. Each match linked to a record in the tree (DNA tab) gives the calculated common ancestor and their places; colour by group or by shared cM. The names of the matches (often living) are only written if you tick the box.

column2: How do I see on a map what I have already searched and what is missing?
column3: Charts → New → Maps → “🔎 Map of your research” → “From the app”: your record indexes (registers consulted), the communes of your search sweeps and the records your ancestors are missing (“What’s missing?”). Green = all seen, orange = partly, red = gaps to cover; choose the kind of record and the period in the settings. A click on a commune: what has been seen and what is missing, with “↗ Open”.

column2: How do I see a heat map decade by decade?
column3: Charts → New → Maps → “🔥 Heat map over time” → “From the app”. The ▶ slider under the drawing (the same as for all diagrams) goes through the decades; in the settings: the decade alone or everything up to it, the same scale for all or one for each.

column2: How do I hide the weather (everywhere, for one person or for one event)?
column3: Everywhere: Settings → Data → “🌦 Weather of the past” → “Weather on records”: Always, On hover or Never; below, the kinds of events (birth, baptism, marriage, death, burial, census…). For one person or a single event: right-click on the badge (or ⋯ in the details, or ⋯ of the “🌦 Weather of their life” block) → “🙈 Hide the weather for this event” or “… for this person”, with “↶ Undo”. Everything hidden is found in the settings, under “Hidden weather”, and shows again with a click on ×. The “Weather of their life” block can also be moved or hidden like the other blocks of the record.

column2: Why does the altitude of a place matter for the weather?
column3: In the mountains, a nearby station in the plain does not tell the weather higher up: the app adds 1 km of distance per 10 m of difference in altitude and never says “Measured” when the difference exceeds 150 m. Each place automatically gets the altitude from the relief map (a grid of about 1 km taken from the Copernicus DEM, supplied with the weather, for France, Belgium, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Germany, Portugal, the United Kingdom, Poland, Denmark, Czechia and Slovakia, islands included; outside France, Belgium, Switzerland and Luxembourg, only the altitude, no weather without the Europe pack), shown as “≈ 312 m (relief map)” in grey. To correct it: Charts → Places → the commune, “Altitude” box (in metres), or “⛰ Altitude of the place” in the details of a day; “↺ Put back the map altitude” returns to the automatic value. The day’s details give the altitude of the station and yours (“Station: Chamonix, 1,042 m — your place ≈ 1,035 m”).

column2: How do I give the time of the record for the weather?
column3: In the event window, “Time of the event” box: write it as in the record (“at 3 o’clock in the morning”, “14:30”). Below, the app says how it understood it and converts it to world time: local solar time before 1891, Paris time until 1911, German time in the occupied zone (1940–1944), then summer time (and the rules of Belgium, Switzerland and Luxembourg). It takes the nearest value (since 1940); before 1940, only the day. The time as written does not change.
